Is Spotify Technology SA a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?
Eric Volkman, The Motley Fool
Sun, October 25, 2026 at 4:00 AM PDT 5 min read
SPOT
^GSPC
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Spotify Technology (NYSE:SPOT) not only saw its third-quarter headline net income fall, but it also whiffed on the consensus analyst estimate. Given that, you'd imagine that investors would have reacted by aggressively selling the music streamer's stock. Well, you'd be very wrong.

The opposite occurred on Thursday after the company published its earnings release -- market players couldn't wait to buy its stock, and it handily beat the S&P 500 index, rising nearly 4%. On Friday, it ticked higher. Let's look at the company's numbers and tease out why it scored such a big win from an ostensibly losing quarter.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Music to their ears

Spotify's quarter was headed by a revenue line that hit almost 5 billion euros ($5.6 billion), for robust year-over-year growth of 16%. By far the bulk of the company's top line comes from its premium services; the take from these rose by 17% to nearly 4.5 billion euros ($5 billion). The remainder came from ad-supported offerings, which collectively rose 10% to 482 million euros ($540 million).

Spotify also managed to grow both its total user base and the crucial segment of that population, premium-service subscribers. The company's total monthly active user (MAU) count rose 11% to 788 million, while the premium subscriber tally increased 9% to 306 million.

Attributable net income, however, went in the opposite direction. It fell to 518 million euros ($580 million) from the year-ago profit of 899 million euros ($1 billion). On a per-share basis, the former result was 2.48 euros ($2.78).

While that revenue number was essentially in line with the consensus analyst estimate, Spotify fell short on profitability. Analysts tracking the stock were modeling net income of 2.84 euros ($3.18) for the quarter.

That bottom-line swoon looked ugly on paper, but it wasn't as grim as it appeared. In the third quarter of 2025, the company benefited enormously from significant finance income derived from share, bond, and warrant valuations, which affected the accounting. It also recorded a 72 million euro ($81 million) tax benefit during that period.

Spotify watchers are aware that these items distorted the 2025 frame's profitability, so the year-over-year drop wasn't particularly concerning to them. They were also impressed that the company topped its guidance for operating income, which came in at 672 million euros ($753 million), and notched a new record for gross margin at 33%. And for a stock increasingly evaluated on free cash flow (FCF), the 735 million euros ($823 million) in FCF it generated during the quarter was heartening.

What Happened?

Analysts raised their Spotify Technology (SPOT:NYSE) price targets on October 22 and 23, yet three of the new targets still sit below the stock's closing price. Shares jumped 11.10% to $583.66 on October 22 after a third-quarter report that beat subscriber guidance and forecast fourth-quarter profit above estimates, on a day the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6%. The move took the stock from about 9.5% below its 2025 year-end close of $580.71 to about 0.5% above it.

Three New Targets Already Trail the Stock

Benzinga's October 23 roundup lists three changes: Cantor Fitzgerald to $550 from $490 and Rosenblatt to $576 from $527, both Neutral, and Guggenheim to $650 from $575 with a Buy. Cantor had cut its target to $490 from $530 on October 12, per TipRanks. Pivotal Research moved to $460 from $420 with a Hold, about 21% below the close, per TipRanks, which also reported Barclays at $650 and Wells Fargo at $660. Raymond James went to $625, per StreetInsider.

Whatever moved those targets, it was not a bigger revenue forecast. TIKR's consensus for fiscal 2027 revenue rose only 0.31% between September 30 and October 23, to about €22.4 billion, while fiscal 2026 slipped 0.13%.

Spotify Analyst Estimates Trend – Revenue (TIKR)

TIKR's Street mean stood at $611.77 on October 22, about $28 above the close, within a range of $459.79 to $720.89. The rating mix shifted between September 30 and October 22, from 24 Buys, 8 Outperforms and 7 Holds to 22 Buys, 9 Outperforms and 9 Holds. The quarter itself missed on two lines: revenue by 0.2%, and GAAP earnings per share of €2.48 against €2.81, a gap TIKR's earnings-day coverage traced to items below operating income.

Spotify Street Targets (TIKR)
Spotify's Co-CEO Bets It Will Be the Last Subscription Users Cancel

Analyst Rich Greenfield asked on the call whether AI agents that compare prices and cancel unused subscriptions could turn Spotify into an interchangeable back-end pipe. Co-CEO Gustav Söderström answered that Spotify has run in the background of Google Maps and Waze for years and grew through it, because the business earns money even when its app is not on screen.

He said more than 100 million users use Spotify roughly 28 days a month, then added: "It's a bold bet but I think on that list of things that you unsubscribe from, Spotify is going to be the last thing that you unsubscribe from." That is a management prediction, not churn data, but heavy daily use is what an agent hunting for forgotten subscriptions would spare.

Spotify Technology SPOT shares climbed 11% on Thursday after the music-streaming giant reported third-quarter results, highlighted by steady subscriber growth, record gross margins and an increasing focus on artificial intelligence (AI).

Revenue Growth and Record Gross Margin

Spotify reported revenue of nearly €5 billion (about $5.6 billion), broadly in line with market expectations. Premium subscription revenue grew 17% year over year, while ad-supported revenue increased 10%.

Spotify came out with quarterly earnings of $2.85 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.1 per share while it fell from the year-ago level of $3.83 per share. Spotify posted revenues of $5.72 billion in September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.70 billion.

However, gross margin reached a record 33%, slightly exceeding Wall Street's estimate of 32.9%. The stock surged 11% during Thursday's trading session. SPOT is now up by only 1.5% for the year 2026.

Subscriber Growth Remains Strong

Spotify continued to expand its user base, with monthly active users rising 11% year over year to 788 million. The company expects monthly active users to reach 818 million in the fourth quarter, while revenue is projected to grow about 15%.

AI Becomes a Bigger Part of Spotify's Strategy

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping Spotify's efforts to improve user engagement and personalization. During the quarter, the company introduced a taste profile feature for U.S. premium subscribers, offering insights into their musical preferences. It also integrated its service with Meta's Muse (read: Should You Tap Meta ETFs on Muse's Success or Wait on the Sidelines?).

However, investors questioned whether AI assistants could weaken Spotify's direct relationship with customers by comparing prices, services and usage across platforms.

Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström dismissed these concerns, drawing a parallel with Spotify's existing integrations with Google Maps and Waze. He noted that users have accessed Spotify through these services during their commutes for years without undermining its business model, as mentioned on Yahoo Finance.

Upbeat Outlook

Spotify guided for €820 million of fourth-quarter operating income. The company's fourth-quarter guidance is expected to be 33.8%, up from 33.1% a year earlier.

For the fourth quarter, Spotify expects 316 million subscribers and €5.2 billion of revenue. The revenue figure is a bit below the €5.24 billion analysts expected, according to Bloomberg's consensus, but the subscriber target is above it, per Tikr, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

Spotify Technology S.A. SPOT used its third-quarter 2026 earnings call to emphasize improving advertising trends, subscriber resilience and a slower pace of expense growth.

Reported earnings of $2.85 per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.1, while revenues of $5.72 billion exceeded the $5.7 billion estimate. Management emphasized future engagement and profitability.

Spotify Technology Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Spotify Technology Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Spotify Technology price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Spotify Technology Quote

SPOT Projects More Growth and Higher Margins in Q4

Chief financial officer Christian Luiga forecast 818 million monthly active users for the fourth quarter, an increase of 30 million, alongside 316 million Premium subscribers, reflecting 10 million net additions.

Luiga guided to €5.2 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, a 33.8% gross margin and €820 million in operating income. Pricing actions and Audiobooks+ add-ons support the revenue outlook.

He said that operating expense growth peaked in the third quarter and should moderate from the fourth quarter into 2027. He cautioned that seasonality and investment timing affect quarterly margins.

Spotify's Advertising Rebuild Gains Traction

Co-CEO Alex Norström said that constant-currency advertising revenue growth accelerated to 9% in the third quarter from 3% in each of the preceding two quarters.

During questions about the advertising recovery, Norström pointed to easier automated buying, improved measurement and greater demand for audio advertisements. Podcast sponsorships contributed.

Luiga said that the company expects to move closer to double-digit advertising growth in the fourth quarter. He noted that advertising represents 10% of revenue, limiting its immediate companywide impact.

SPOT Positions AI Agents as a Distribution Channel

Co-CEO Gustav Söderström argued that integrations with third-party AI agents can broaden access without transferring Spotify's customer listening activity or proprietary taste data to those services.

Addressing concerns about becoming a replaceable back-end provider, Söderström explained that playback remains within Spotify and its recommendation systems continue to interpret user preferences.

He highlighted double-digit gains in content discovery from Spotify's large taste model. Almost 40 million Premium users listen to mixed playlists, with consumption up 90% quarter over quarter.

Spotify Takes Audiobooks Into New Markets

Norström described the expansion of audiobooks from 22 markets to more than 180 by year-end as an opportunity to increase listening days, retention and subscriber lifetime value.

During the discussion of rollout economics, he said audiobook listenership had increased 40%, and add-ons were showing encouraging monetization results. Luiga said initial expansion expenses are included in margin guidance.

Söderström also discussed bringing the Spotify Partner Program to 35 additional markets and introducing creator memberships, widening opportunities for creators to monetize dedicated audiences.

SPOT Refines Its Subscriber Conversion Strategy

Norström emphasized durable subscriber demand across regions, while Luiga reported 306 million Premium subscribers and 788 million monthly active users at quarter-end.

Asked about changes to the free tier in India and Indonesia, Norström described adjustments to sign-up data, advertising load and device experiences aimed at improving retention and eventual monetization.

On pricing, Norström said that Spotify seeks to add value before monetizing through subscription increases, add-ons and advertising. The objective remains improving value to subscribers while expanding revenue opportunities.

Spotify Balances Buybacks With Strategic Flexibility

Luiga mentioned that Spotify repurchased 2.2 million shares for $1.1 billion through Oct. 21, offsetting employee-equity dilution and beginning to return excess cash to shareholders.

With €9.9 billion in cash and equivalents at quarter-end and no debt apart from lease liabilities, management retained flexibility for organic investment and acquisitions.

Norström reiterated that internal growth opportunities and selective acquisitions take priority over additional repurchases. Luiga emphasized opportunistic capital deployment.

SPOT Maintains Its Focus on Durable Expansion

Across the call, management presented advertising improvement, broader content offerings and AI-powered personalization as ways to deepen engagement while protecting recurring subscription growth.

Executives also reinforced expense moderation and margin discipline extending into 2027. Their near-term focus remains delivering fourth-quarter targets while funding new products.

Zacks Rank and Style Scores Point to Caution

SPOT carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), indicating an unfavorable earnings-estimate revision profile. Its Growth Score of A signals stronger growth characteristics, while the Value Score of D and Momentum score of D point to weaker readings in those categories.

The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Friday, Oct, 23 2026

US stocks look set for a cautiously positive open, with S&P 500 futures hovering slightly higher. The single driver this morning is labor strength, as fresh jobless claims signal a still resilient employment backdrop.

Initial unemployment claims came in at 194,000 for the week ended October 17, the lowest level since July. Continuing claims held at 1.728 million. Together, those figures point to limited layoffs and ongoing income support for households.

A labor market that tight keeps wage pressures in focus and can keep borrowing costs sensitive to any upside inflation surprises. At the same time, steady paychecks support revenue expectations in consumer facing businesses and help justify risk exposure in economically sensitive areas.

The unresolved question is how long the Federal Reserve can tolerate this level of labor resilience without shifting its rate stance. This afternoon's US manufacturing and services PMI readings could quickly reset that debate if activity diverges from expectations.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

PG&E (PCG)

PG&E reaffirmed its 2026 and 2027 non GAAP core earnings guidance and flagged a US$2b cut to its 2027 capital plan, along with a 2% to 4% target reduction in non fuel operating and maintenance expenses. Management is also weighing a possible separation of the gas unit if wildfire policy does not change, while lobbying for legislative relief.

Alnylam reported early Phase 1b data for brezosiran in Huntington's disease, showing robust, dose dependent lowering of mutant huntingtin protein in cerebrospinal fluid with encouraging safety. Investors will likely focus on how aggressively the buyback is used and how it fits alongside spending on pipeline and other long term goals.

Earnings season in the US shifts into high gear over the next few sessions, with heavyweights reporting against a backdrop of closely watched growth and inflation data.

S&P Global US PMIs Fri 23 Oct. The manufacturing consensus sits at 55.5 after a 55.9 print. A stronger reading would underline firm demand that can keep borrowing costs sensitive, while a softer figure would ease pressure on rate expectations.

Alphabet (GOOGL) Q3 2026 results Wed 28 Oct. Ad revenue trends across search and YouTube will show how marketing budgets are holding up, which influences expectations for other internet platforms and media exposed to the same advertisers.

Sector & Industry Watch

Energy & Oil and Gas: Higher oil keeps cash engines humming

Energy and Oil and Gas are both in the green over the past week and month, on top of strong 1 year returns. Elevated oil prices tied to Middle East risks plus US pipeline and LNG build outs from groups like Kinder Morgan and Cheniere keep cash flow stories front and center. The trend check is the next US crude and product inventory report, which shows whether tight supply is still offsetting demand worries.

Tech & Semiconductors: AI buildout strong, funding questions louder

Tech and Semiconductors have slipped over the last 7 and 30 days despite solid gains over 1 year, as investors react to talk of an AI funding squeeze and mixed earnings reactions in chip names. Headlines around Nvidia, Tesla, Western Digital and Lam Research all point to heavy dependence on AI data center spending that now gets questioned more closely. For anyone holding broad tech or chip ETFs, the key catalyst is upcoming US PMIs this afternoon, since softer activity can quickly cool enthusiasm for new cloud and data center projects.

The first drop in the 30 year US mortgage rate in nine weeks to 7.32% helps, yet pending home sales are at record lows and job data remain firm, so rate cuts are not a given. Consumer Staples & Food, Beverage & Tobacco: Defensive corner attracts steady interest

Consumer Staples along with Food, Beverage & Tobacco are up over the week, month and 1 year, offering a contrast to the recent US Market pullback. Deals like PepsiCo's long renewal with Taco Bell and buybacks or capital injections at Vylor, Zevia and Vita Coco show companies leaning into brand strength and balance sheets rather than big cyclical bets. For portfolios using these groups as ballast, the next clear catalyst is US PCE inflation next week, since a firm print tends to keep demand for more predictable earnings streams in place.

Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals & Biotech: Trial wins keep sector in focus

Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech are both higher across all reported periods, supported by a steady run of positive data and deal news from companies like Vera Therapeutics, Alnylam, Gilead, AbbVie and Moderna's partner Merck. These stories remind investors that drug pipelines and approvals often matter more here than monthly macro swings. The main near term sector driver is how markets digest today's strong US jobless claims alongside next week's PCE inflation, because stickier inflation and solid jobs usually keep interest in sectors where earnings feel less tied to day to day consumer spending.

Music fans are flocking to Spotify

Spotify's monthly active users (MAUs) grew 11% year over year to 788 million in the third quarter.

The audio streaming platform is successfully enticing free users to become paying customers to access upgraded features, such as ad-free listening, offline downloads, and higher quality audio. Premium subscribers increased 9% to 306 million.

In all, Spotify's revenue climbed 16% to 5 billion euros, or roughly $5.6 billion.

Better still, Spotify is growing more profitable as it expands its subscriber base. Gross margin improved by 1.4 percentage points to 33%. That helped to drive its operating income up by 15% to 672 million euros ($754 million).

Management sees more gains ahead

Spotify sees its MAUs and premium subscribers rising to 818 million and 316 million, respectively, in the fourth quarter. The company, in turn, expects to generate revenue of 5.2 billion euros and operating income of 820 million euros.

Spotify has a simple and effective formula for expansion. It continually seeks new ways to add value for listeners and artists, thereby attracting new users who then spend more time on its platform.

Spotify plans to roll out its audiobook offerings to over 180 markets by the end of the year. It's also launching new tools to help creators better monetize their work.

"Every time we expand what's on Spotify, we bring in new listeners and give existing ones more reasons to come back, almost every day," Co-CEO Alex Norstrom said.
